terms.comment: A table for writing: mēnsa is any table, and scrīptōrius, for writing, is Celsus’s adjective (ātrāmentum scrīptōrium, writing ink: Cels. 6.4, Lewis & Short). Traupman gives mēnsa scrīptōria scholae for a school desk (p. 29).
Classically a platform of boards for actors, lectures and disputations (Lewis & Short); Traupman’s word for the teacher’s desk.

phrases.latin: Quīdam sedent ad mēnsam, et scrībunt; ipse corrigit mendās.
phrases.english: Some sit at the table and write; the master corrects their mistakes.

sources: Lewis & Short: mensa · Lewis & Short: scriptorius · Lewis & Short: pulpitum
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 29, 123, 303, checked against the searchable text of the book (9 November 2026).
